physics_goals.quote: very light particles which can point the way toward unknown physics phenomena, like e.g. the dark matter in the Universe
physics_goals.value: Search for axion-like particles and other very light, weakly interacting particles using a light-shining-through-a-wall technique

summary.plain: ALPS II shines a laser at a light-tight wall to see whether a tiny fraction can pass through as an undetectable particle and turn back into light on the far side. This would reveal new, very light particles related to dark matter. It has been operating at DESY since 2023.
summary.technical: Light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) experiment at DESY reusing decommissioned superconducting HERA dipole magnets and matched optical build-up/regeneration cavities, successor to ALPS I (completed 2010); TDR submitted 2012-08, operating (data taking) since 2023-05-23.

unique_capabilities.quote: The ALPS I experiment at DESY set the world-wide best laboratory limits for WISPs in 2010, improving previous results by a factor of 10. After its completion the ALPS collaboration decided to continue looking for WISPs by designing the ALPS II experiment for probing further into regions where there are strong astrophysical hints for their existence.
unique_capabilities.value: Reuses decommissioned superconducting HERA dipole magnets in matched build-up and regeneration optical cavities to boost sensitivity to photon-into-WISP oscillation
